subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: CorrespondingBinder.BindAddCorresponding (lines 25-29) -> Bind (49-81) -> CorrMatch (91-151), producing BoundCorresponding(CorrVerb.Add, hoists, pairs, rounding, sizeErr); the store side is the same ArithmeticEmitter.StoreArith the non-CORR forms use. MATCHED, first sentence: 'data items in identifier-4 are added to and stored in corresponding items in identifier-5' -- each pair is emitted as `dst = dst + src`, i.e. the SOURCE group supplies the addend and the TARGET group is both sending and receiving, which is the direction the rule states (and the mirror of the SUBTRACT direction pinned by CorrespondingDifferentialTests.SubtractCorr_TargetMinusSource_CorrToken). Value evidence: conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/corresponding_rounded_mode adds SRC.P=1.25 and SRC.Q=1.21 into DST.P/DST.Q (both PIC 9V9, initially 0) giving 1.2/1.2 truncated and 1.3/1.2 rounded -- the expected values derived from the rule plus Sec.14.7.4, not from an oracle; AddCorresponding_RoundedAppliesToEachPair adds into non-zero receivers (1.0+1.25 -> 2.3, 1.0+2.34 -> 3.3), which is the `operand-1 + operand-2` shape with a non-trivial operand-2. UNVERIFIED HALF: the rule's second paragraph, 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the result of the addition is equivalent to (operand-1 + operand-2)' -- STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind (DataBinder.cs:318-320; docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 2 'Not claimed'), and no ADD CORRESPONDING golden runs under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a STANDARD-DECIMAL ADD CORRESPONDING golden whose per-pair SDIDI result differs from the native Int128 one. || UPHELD. I read CorrespondingEmitter.Emit (CorrespondingEmitter.cs:21-47) myself, which the record did not cite but which is where GR3's direction actually lands: `string op = c.Verb is CorrVerb.Add ? "+" : "-"` then `StoreArith(p.Target, num.Combine(num.FieldNum(p.Target), op, num.FieldNum(p.Source), rcv), c.Rounding)` -- target on the left, source on the right, exactly 'added to and stored in corresponding items in identifier-5'. Verified AddCorresponding_RoundedAppliesToEachPair is spec-derived: it is `AssertOutput(src, "23\n33")` with the expected values derived in a comment from Sec.14.7.4.3 r1, and only THEN also AssertSameAsLegacy -- the AssertOutput half qualifies. || REFUTED (a second unverified half, and a narrower edition footprint than the row claims): (a) tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance/CompilerUnderTest.cs:115 declares `WiseOwlCobolCompiler(int dialectLevel = 85)`, so every AddCorresponding_* xunit case runs at COBOL-85 ONLY, and conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/corresponding_rounded_mode is 2014-gated (it writes ROUNDED MODE IS). GR3 therefore has value evidence at 85 and 2014 and NONE at 2002 or 2023; the editions field stays 85,2002,2014,2023 because the rule has no edition delta (Annex E lists no ADD change), but the coverage does not span it. (b) code-location moved from the emitter-shared StoreArith to BindAddCorresponding, the symbol that actually decides Format 3's operand roles. PB228 (2026-10-16), SECOND PARAGRAPH NOW PINNED: 2014/pb228_add_standard_decimal's CORR leg adds SRC.P = 0.9996 to DST.P = 10**30 + 4 under STANDARD-DECIMAL: (operand-1 + operand-2) = 10**30 + 4.9996 needs 35 digits, rounds NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO (11.9.11.2 GR3a) to 10**30 + 5.000 and truncates to ...0005, where exact native arithmetic would store ...0004; the Q pair and the unpartnered S/T items pin the per-pair selection. The 2002 gap is closed too: 2002/pb228_add_corresponding_values pins GR3/GR5 under native arithmetic at COBOL-2002 (a nested pair, a non-numeric non-pair per 14.7.6 rule 3, truncation, a signed result), so GR3 now has value evidence at 85 (xunit), 2002, 2014.
